title: Revit connector how-to document
description: One task, the shortest correct path to doing it on a given Revit version, and the mistakes that path avoids. Interchange format for the how-to corpus (see howto-corpus-design.md). One document per JSONL line. Unknown top-level fields are ALLOWED so an older broker can still read a newer corpus (it ignores what it does not know and reports the newer corpus_version in guidance); the fields it does know are validated strictly.

schema_version.description: Schema revision this document was written against. A broker validates the fields it knows and ignores the rest; when the corpus declares a schema_version above the broker's, every response says so in guidance (howto-corpus-newer-than-broker).

id.description: Stable kebab-case slug, unique across the shared corpus. A local document with the same id overrides the shared one for that user (supersedes_shared on the hit).

kind.description: howto: a working path to a task. negative: the API does NOT offer this; here is what to do instead (the ranker always returns something, so 'stop looking' must be a document). pitfall: a single mistake and its fix, without a full task script.

title.description: Short noun phrase, the way a person would name the example.

task.description: The task in agent language, one to three plain sentences naming the element types and the operation. Primary embedding text for search.

summary.description: Optional: the approach in prose, for describe_howto. Not indexed.

queries.description: Recorded phrasings from real sessions. Misses are the most valuable rows: they are where API search failed and this document earns its keep.

hit.description: Phrasings that found the right member or this document.

miss.description: Phrasings that did NOT surface the answer, with what they surfaced instead.

members.description: Fully-qualified Namespace.Type.Member names the script calls (describe_function's 'member' shape; constructors as Type.#ctor, generic arity with a backtick). Indexed for exact-name hits and used to cross-link API results. Empty is legal for kind=negative, whose 'related' member (the one that does NOT exist) goes in pitfalls[].members as free text.

script.description: The C# script body in the connector's dialect: ambient transaction (never open your own), `Document`/`UIApplication`/`Connector` globals, `return` a value. Required for kind=howto; optional otherwise. 16 KB bound.

symptom.description: What the agent sees: the error text, the wrong result, the silent nothing.

members.description: Members this pitfall is about, when different from the document's. Free text (a negative how-to names a member that does not exist).

pitfalls.description: One entry per mistake the path avoids. Indexed text.

tags.description: Free-form facets (walls, views, sheets, worksharing, transactions). Not indexed for ranking; for browsing and de-duplication.

api_since.description: Declared hint: first Revit version whose API offers the members used. Not verification.

api_until.description: Declared hint: last Revit version before a used member was removed or deprecated.

kind.description: harness/validation-corpus: extracted from a repo test. submission: arrived through submit_howto and the review queue. local: written by submit_howto into the user's own corpus, never reviewed. maintainer: authored directly in the repo.

ref.description: Where it came from: a test function name (harness), an issue URL (submission), a validation-corpus case number.

reviewed_by.description: GitHub login of the reviewer, or 'review-agent', set when accepted into the shared corpus. Never set on a local document.

submitter.description: Optional public handle the submitter chose to attach. Never an email or machine name; the scrubber removes those.

supersedes.description: id of the document this one replaces. The shared corpus is append-only; an edit is a new document pointing at the old one, and search hides superseded documents.

text.description: The query as sent to search_functions or search_howto.

rank.description: For hits: the rank the answer appeared at.

surfaced.description: For misses: what came back instead, in a few words.

ranker.description: The ranker value the response reported, so a recorded rank is read against the ranker that produced it. Episodes recorded before #107 shipped were served by the add-in's tiered ranker, which is what keyword-fallback names today.
